# `prepayment` commands

## `prepayment apply`

Use held prepayment money on an invoice: a credit memo draws it from the receipts, oldest first, and is applied to the invoice in the same step. Draws from the document the invoice was made from by default; or name a document, the customer (money not on any document) or the receipts. Amount defaults to the lesser of what is held and what the invoice owes; more than either is refused (E_APPLIED_EXCEEDS_TOTAL). This is also how a kept fee becomes income: invoice the fee, then apply the deposit to it. Undo with `prepayment unapply`. Example: {"invoice": "1043", "document": "work-order 1002", "amount": "150.00"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/prepayment.apply` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow prepayment apply --invoice DEMO-SALE-INV-ACTIVE --document "estimate DEMO-WORK-EST-1B" --amount 150.00 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "prepayment apply", "input": {"invoice": "DEMO-SALE-INV-ACTIVE", "document": "estimate DEMO-WORK-EST-1B", "amount": "150.00"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | `--document` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Draw from the money held on this customer-work document (and, for a work order, on the estimate it came from): its id or kind and number. |
| `customer` | `--customer` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Draw from the money held for this customer or job and not on any document: ID or full name. |
| `receipts` | `--receipts` | array[string] \| null | no | yes | null | Draw from exactly these prepayment receipts, in this order: IDs or numbers. |
| `invoice` | `--invoice` | string | yes | no | — | Invoice the held money pays: ID or number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `amount` | `--amount` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Amount to use. Defaults to the lesser of what is held and what the invoice still owes. |
| `date` | `--date` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Date of the draw and its application. Defaults to the invoice date, or the latest receipt drawn when that is later. |

## `prepayment attach`

Move what a prepayment receipt still holds to one of its customer's documents (an accepted estimate, a work order or a sales order), or back to the customer when no document is named. What was already drawn stays where it went. The receipt's history keeps every move. Example: {"receipt": "57", "document": "work-order 1002"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | ledger.post and customer-work standard role |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Additional resources | customer-work: standard |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/prepayment.attach` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow prepayment attach 57 --document "work-order DEMO-WORK-WO-2" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "prepayment attach", "input": {"receipt": "57", "document": "work-order DEMO-WORK-WO-2"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `receipt` | `RECEIPT` | string | yes | no | — | The prepayment receipt: sales receipt ID or number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |
| `document` | `--document` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The customer-work document the money is held on: its id, or its kind and number such as "estimate 1001", "work-order 1002" or "sales-order 1003" (a bare number works when only one document carries it). An estimate must be accepted. Omit it to hold the money for the customer again. |

## `prepayment receive`

A customer prepayment is a deposit, down payment or retainer: money paid before the work bills. It is held on the Customer Prepayments liability (set up on first use), never income, until an invoice uses it or it is paid back. Take one: name the customer or job, or the document it is for (an accepted estimate, a work order or a sales order, as "estimate 1001", "work-order 1002" or "sales-order 1003"), the amount, and optionally date, payment method, reference, deposit-to (default Undeposited Funds, banked later with `deposit post`), class and memo. It is an ordinary sales receipt with one Customer Prepayment line: it prints as the customer's receipt and deposits, corrects, voids and deletes as any sales receipt, while nothing is drawn from it. An invoice made from the document (`estimate invoice`, `work-order invoice`, `sales-order invoice`) uses it by itself; `prepayment apply` uses it on any invoice. Example: {"document": "work-order 1002", "amount": "200.00", "payment_method": "Check", "reference": "4471"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/prepayment.receive` |
| External binary body | none |


An estimate must be accepted. The customer is the document's. |

## `prepayment refund`

Pay held prepayment money back to the customer: a credit memo draws it from the receipts, oldest first, and a customer refund pays it from the bank account named, by the payment method named. Name the document, the customer (money not on any document) or the receipts; amount defaults to everything held there. Example: {"document": "estimate 1001", "bank_account": "Checking", "payment_method": "Check", "check_number": "2210"}.

## `prepayment show`

|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | ledger.read |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/prepayment.show` |
| External binary body | none |

## `prepayment unapply`

Undo a draw: unapply its credit memo from the invoice (or void the refund that paid it back) and void the credit memo, in one step, returning the money to its receipts. A reason is required. Refused when the draw was applied inside a closed period, since its undoing carries the application date: correct it in an open period instead. Example: {"draw": "1044"}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | ledger.post |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/prepayment.unapply` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow prepayment unapply 1044 --reason "Applied to the wrong invoice" --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "prepayment unapply", "input": {"draw": "1044"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `draw` | `DRAW` | string | yes | no | — | The drawing credit memo, as `prepayment show` or the invoice lists it: ID or number.; minimum length 1; maximum length 1000 |

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_AMOUNT_PRECISION` | The amount has more decimal places than the currency allows. |
| `E_APPLICATION_INACTIVE` | This application is already unapplied or its payment is voided. |
| `E_APPLIED_EXCEEDS_TOTAL` | The corrected total is below active settlement capacity. |
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_DUPLICATE_NUMBER` | That document number is already used in this document's number series. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_HAS_APPLICATIONS` | Unapply the active settlements before this change. |
| `E_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH` | That idempotency key was used for a different command or input. |
| `E_INACTIVE_REFERENCE` | A new or changed reference must name an active record. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERIOD_CLOSED` | An affected accounting date is in a closed period. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_PREVIEW_STALE` | The resolved document facts changed since preview; preview again before saving. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VALUE_RANGE` | The value is outside its allowed range or storage bounds. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
